candidate.answerReason: The large semicircle has N times the combined area of the small semicircles. The given ratio makes that same area 19 times A, so N = 19.

methods.label: Compare the areas using their radii
methods.explanation:
The small diameters fit end to end, so the large radius is \(N\) times a small radius. Let a small radius be \(r>0\), and let one small semicircle have area \(a=\frac12\pi r^2\). The large semicircle then has area
\[
\frac12\pi(Nr)^2=N^2a,
\]
while the combined small area is \(A=Na\).

The ratio \(A:B=1:18\) means \(B=18A\), so the whole large semicircle has area \(A+B=19A\). Therefore
\[
N^2a=19Na.
\]
Since \(N\) is a positive integer and \(a>0\), we may divide by \(Na\), giving \(\boxed{N=19}\), choice \(\mathrm{D}\).
methods.levelReason: Uses the circle-area formula, the radius-diameter relationship, and a simple area ratio, all within AMC 10 scope.
